summary: The suite is 17 files driven by one entry point, `selftest.sh`, which runs 16 unit gates (15 python + 1 shell) and then, unless `--quick`, one real 9,000-token/2-epoch CPU training run plus one resume, checked by 13 fixed-string greps, and finally one `compare.py` invocation checked by a single grep. Nothing else in the repo invokes it (`preflight.sh`, `equiv.sh`, `rerun.sh` do not). Verified state: all 16 unit gates pass, the full end-to-end run passes, exit 0. Roughly 420 static assertions live in the python files, 110 of them in `resume_test.py` alone. Coverage is deliberately split into three styles: real-import (`mem_evict_test`→memory.py, `compare_test`→compare.py, `tok_test`→tokenizer.py, `growth_test`→self_organize.py), AST-lift of module-level defs (`proj_test`, `cap_test`, `ramp_test`, `blowup_test`, `curve_test`, parts of `resume_test`), and raw-source `exec` against hand-written stubs (`domain_test`, `corpus_test`, most of `resume_test`). There are 17 source-text/AST anchors into `self_organize.py`; every one currently resolves and is unique except `"    if USE_TOK:"` (4 occurrences, disambiguated only by search offset), and a rebuild that renames a banner comment or moves a function out of module scope breaks them. The suite is honest about restating code in several places, but four of its headline claims overstate what is actually checked, and its own end-to-end run reports 14 ARMED AND INERT mechanisms — including several that the unit tests exist to protect — while passing. `world_model.py`, `verification.py`, `datastream.py`, `vocab.py`, `holdout.py`, `prompt.py`, `fetch_*.py`, and every other shell script have no test at all.

levers.name: SELFTEST_DEVICE
levers.effect: Device for the two end-to-end training runs. Defaults to cpu. $DEVICE is deliberately NOT consulted, so an ambient DEVICE=cuda (which longrun.sh exports) cannot put a selftest job on the GPU.

levers.name: SELFTEST_DIR
levers.effect: Where artefacts go. Unset -> a fresh mktemp -d. Everything the log assertions grep lives under it.

levers.name: SELFTEST_DATA
levers.effect: DATA_DIR for the end-to-end runs; defaults to `data`. With a missing or tiny corpus the two runs fail and 13 log assertions cascade.

levers.name: FAB_GROW
levers.effect: Read by PlateauGrowth.__init__ from the real environment. growth_test.py imports self_organize and does NOT stub _env, so FAB_GROW=0 in the ambient environment turns off every growth path and produces 5 spurious failures plus 2 vacuously-passing 'no false positive' checks.
levers.owner: growth_test.py (should stub _env as ramp_test.py and resume_test.py do)
levers.evidence: self_organize.py:2938 `s.grow_on = bool(int(_env("FAB_GROW", 1)))`; verified: `FAB_GROW=0 python3 growth_test.py` exits 1 with 5 failures

levers.name: FAB_RAMP_LATCH
levers.effect: Also read by PlateauGrowth.__init__ from the real environment; 0 restores the never-terminating ramp. Ambient FAB_RAMP_LATCH=0 makes growth_test.py fail 3 checks.
levers.evidence: self_organize.py:2939 `s.latch = bool(int(_env("FAB_RAMP_LATCH", 1)))`; verified: `FAB_RAMP_LATCH=0 python3 growth_test.py` exits 1

levers.name: MEM_WRONG_READ
levers.effect: Read by EditableMemory.__init__ from os.environ. mem_evict_test.py constructs the store without setting it, so an ambient MEM_WRONG_READ=0 makes wrong_gates_reads() fail and the whole gate exit 1.
levers.owner: mem_evict_test.py (should pass it explicitly or set os.environ before import)

levers.name: DATA_MODE / BENCH / WORLD_MODEL / FABRIC / EXPERTS / TOKENIZER
levers.effect: growth_test.py sets these with os.environ.setdefault before importing self_organize, so an ambient value WINS. FABRIC=1 ambient changes what module-scope self_organize builds during the import (it still passed here).
levers.evidence: growth_test.py:21-23; verified: `FABRIC=1 python3 growth_test.py` still passes

levers.name: working directory
levers.effect: Not an env var but behaves as one. domain_test.py, corpus_test.py and resume_test.py open self_organize.py by RELATIVE path, and selftest.sh invokes every gate by bare filename, so the whole suite requires cwd == repo root.
levers.evidence: domain_test.py:47, corpus_test.py:34, resume_test.py:40 `SRC = open("self_organize.py").read()`; verified: `cd /tmp && bash /home/user/LLM-Test/selftest.sh --quick` fails all 16 gates

levers.name: --quick
levers.effect: Skips both end-to-end runs and the compare gate; runs only the 16 unit gates. Everything the DID IT FIRE / FORGOTTEN-EVICTED sections guarantee is skipped.

levers.name: --quiet (levers.py)
levers.effect: Documented as 'drift only'. Currently raises UnboundLocalError before printing any verdict, so the flag is unusable.

levers.name: --write (notes_check.py)
levers.effect: Regenerates notes/CURRENT_DEFAULTS.md from _SPEC instead of failing on drift. Without it, a stale generated file is a hard exit 1.

levers.name: FIX=1 (preflight.sh)
levers.effect: Not part of the test suite but the neighbouring gate; noted because preflight.sh is the file that already contains the cwd fix selftest.sh lacks.

States NOT SIGNIFICANT is the correct answer for two single-seed logs. The tool must and does return NO VERDICT. Misleads anyone reading the gate to understand what it proves.

carry_forward.item: There are exactly 17 anchors from the tests into self_organize.py, and a rebuild breaks every one. Six are AST anchors requiring a name to stay MODULE LEVEL: proj_arith, lift_to, pin_tick, PlateauGrowth (class), blowup_stale, and the four of curve_verdict/bwt_of/forgetting_of/cull_gate_open; plus widen_prefix, _curve_by_step, _load_enc and _lr_at reached the same way. Eleven are raw source-text anchors on exact strings.
carry_forward.why: Moving any of these back into main() or a closure silently or loudly disables between 10 and 110 assertions. Several tests say so in their own refusal messages ('back inside main() it is untestable again').
carry_forward.evidence: proj_test.py:41-45, cap_test.py:27-34, ramp_test.py:33-37, blowup_test.py:47-51, curve_test.py:29-36, lr_test.py:46-51, resume_test.py:68/274/330/838

carry_forward.item: The anchoring convention that survived three separate drift incidents: anchor the START on a distinctive BANNER COMMENT (not an ordinary line, which may repeat), and end at the NEXT banner so that inserting a block between two of them fails LOUDLY with a NameError rather than reporting on the wrong text.
carry_forward.why: Three anchors have already grabbed the wrong span in this project — resume_test twice (a duplicate `_wide_by = 0`; the growth-controller restore landing between two banners) and corpus_test once (the capacity-gate warning landing inside its span). All three failed correctly.

carry_forward.item: `"    if USE_TOK:"` occurs 4 times in self_organize.py and is corpus_test's held-out-tail end anchor, disambiguated only by the search offset from `"    _unshuf = []"`. Every other anchor is unique.
carry_forward.why: An inserted `if USE_TOK:` between lines 1182 and 1199 would silently truncate the block and the test would exec a fragment.
carry_forward.evidence: scripted anchor scan: TAIL start L1182 end L1199, endcount=4; every other anchor endcount=1

carry_forward.item: Build PlateauGrowth the way the CALL SITE does, never from its signature defaults. Signature: cooldown=1500, warmup=2000, burst=3. Call site: FAB_COOLDOWN=400, FAB_WARMUP=300, FAB_BURST=1. resume_test already got burned by this (the first version had ramp=0 and every ramp assertion passed vacuously).
carry_forward.why: growth_test.py and cap_test.py §7 still use the signature values, so their timing claims describe a controller no run builds.

carry_forward.item: mem_evict_test must stay seeded with torch.manual_seed(0). The store's victim sampling calls torch.randint/randperm on the GLOBAL RNG, and unseeded the suite failed 3 times in 20 on unchanged code.
carry_forward.why: A regression test that fails 15% of the time cannot be used to judge a change; the instinct on a red run is to re-run it, which is the instinct that lets a real regression through.

carry_forward.item: The suite must be run from the repo root. domain_test.py, corpus_test.py and resume_test.py open self_organize.py by relative path, and selftest.sh invokes every gate by bare filename. preflight.sh already carries the one-line fix (`cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"`).
carry_forward.why: From any other directory all 16 gates fail with 'can't open file', which reads as catastrophic breakage.
carry_forward.evidence: domain_test.py:47, corpus_test.py:34, resume_test.py:40, preflight.sh:14-15; verified from /tmp

carry_forward.item: selftest.sh must not read $DEVICE. longrun.sh exports DEVICE=cuda, and the suite is meant to be run often and at any time, which is only safe if running it cannot cost anything. SELFTEST_DEVICE is the opt-in.
carry_forward.why: An earlier version used DEVICE=${DEVICE:-cpu} and would have quietly put a training job on the GPU beside an 18-epoch run.

carry_forward.item: Anything selftest.sh does not name explicitly is skipped. Two tests (corpus_test, resume_test) sat unwired for a whole session, silently omitting ~120 checks. The file now states what it deliberately does NOT run and why.
carry_forward.why: 'A TEST NOBODY RUNS IS A TEST THAT DOES NOT EXIST.' A rebuild must re-wire every gate into the entry point or repeat the omission.

carry_forward.item: compare.py pairs runs by the SEED printed on the `[config] EFFECTIVE` line. SEED must stay in _EFF or the regex matches 0 logs and every paired comparison falls back to a filename heuristic or crashes.
carry_forward.why: That regex once matched 0 of 37 real logs while compare_test passed against a fixture the shipped code could not emit.

carry_forward.item: Registry facts the tests depend on: _SPEC has 328 knobs; MIN_PAIRS=3; FAB_COOLDOWN=400; FAB_BURST=1; FAB_WARMUP=300; FAB_RAMP_TO=0.5; FAB_PRESSURE=0.45; GROW_LIFT=0.08; GROW_LIFT_MIN=8; MEM_SRC_FLOOR=0.5; DOM_CULL_FRAC=0.1; FAB_CULL_FRAC=0.02; EXPOSURE_MAX=2.0; EXPOSURE_SKEW=3.0; BLOWUP_RISE=0.5; BLOWUP_STALE=80; CURVE_RISE_BLEWUP=0.5; CURVE_FLAT=0.05; CURVE_TOK_RISE=0.05.
carry_forward.why: blowup_test and curve_test read theirs from source; every other test hardcodes them. A rebuild that changes a default silently invalidates the hardcoding tests without failing them.

carry_forward.item: notes/CURRENT_DEFAULTS.md is GENERATED from _SPEC by `python3 notes_check.py --write` and is the only file in notes/ allowed to state a current default. Everything else must either match _SPEC or read as history.
carry_forward.why: Nine notes stated FAB_N0=3 a week after it became 2048, and that claim was 00_INDEX's 'five things to know before spending any GPU time' item #1.

carry_forward.item: harness_test.sh must SOURCE longrun.sh's functions with sed rather than execute the script, because longrun.sh dispatches on $1 at the bottom and sourcing it whole would start a run.
carry_forward.why: A harness test that can start a training job is not safe to run before every launch.

carry_forward.item: `__UNKNOWN_ARM__` is the sentinel that separates 'defined with no overrides' (base, the control every comparison is measured against) from 'never defined'. Empty is not undefined.
carry_forward.why: Treating empty as missing makes the test fail on the one arm the whole project baselines against; treating undefined as empty runs the defaults under a misspelled arm's log name.

carry_forward.item: The suite currently touches only self_organize.py, compare.py, memory.py, tokenizer.py and longrun.sh. world_model.py, verification.py, datastream.py, vocab.py, holdout.py, prompt.py, cl_bench.py, runs.py, fetch_big.py, fetch_local.py, rescue_ckpt.py, keystone_probe.py, probe_*.py and every shell script but longrun.sh have zero coverage.
carry_forward.why: world_model.py and verification.py are imported at self_organize module scope, so they execute in the end-to-end run with nothing asserted about them; the rest are not exercised at all.
carry_forward.evidence: import/anchor map across all 17 files; self_organize.py:20-22

carry_forward.item: The selftest's end-to-end run uses DOMAINS=eng (NP=1) and resumes at identical geometry, so the DN/CORP realignment, the exposure guard, the held-out-tail check, the fabric widening, the newborn split and the tokenizer cap raise NEVER execute there. All of resume_test's 110 checks and corpus_test's source-block sections are stub-only.
carry_forward.why: A rebuild that changes those paths gets no end-to-end signal at all; the stubs are the entire safety net.
carry_forward.evidence: selftest.sh:114; verified 0 hits for 'WIDENING', 'cap-shaped fabric tensor', 'LIVE here but were not in the checkpoint', 'DROPPED', 'HELD-OUT TAIL IS A BLOCK', 'exposure over the whole run' in both logs of a passing full run

open_questions: Was tok_test's synthetic corpus meant to reach the cap? The docstring quotes real-English reproductions (1845/2048 with 3940 candidates left; 658/4000 with 1866 left) but the shipped 168 kB / 36-distinct-word fixture exhausts at 353 tokens with 0 candidates left, so the headline assertion is satisfied by exhaustion rather than by the fix. A richer fixture, or asserting gate_skipped > 0 in each case, would restore the discrimination.

Should notes/_evidence/ be inside notes_check's scope? It is a chat/commit transcript archive, so excluding it may be intended — but the exclusion is accidental (non-recursive os.listdir), the docstring claims the opposite, and 19 drift lines sit there. Either move it under archive/ or exclude it by name.

Is the unfiltered `_cs` at self_organize.py:6433 deliberate? The blow-up alarm averages absent processes while _curve_by_step filters them for the end-of-run verdict. If unintended, this is the same defect the _curve_by_step fix removed, still live at the other consumer.

Are the 14 ARMED AND INERT mechanisms in the selftest's own run expected at STREAM_LEN=9000/FAB_NMAX=8, or do some of them indicate genuinely dead code? I could not distinguish 'too small to fire' from 'never fires' without a larger run. domains.cull, domains.held, memory.wrong_block and tokenizer.mint_reject are the ones whose unit tests would be most reassuring to see fire once end-to-end.

Should harness_test scrape arms from _flags_for's case labels instead of from preset ARMS= lines? That would raise coverage from 62 to 99 arms. Both checks pass over all 99 today, so the change is free — but I do not know whether some of the 37 uncovered labels are intentionally retired.

Can the two predicates cap_test §6/§7 restate be hoisted to module level, the way lift_to/pin_tick/blowup_stale/cull_gate_open were? Both currently live inside main() (self_organize.py:7397 and :7411), which is exactly the condition every other section of cap_test refuses to accept.

Does anything read compare.py's exit code in practice (a wrapper script, a sweep report)? If so, the 13 unasserted `rc` values in compare_test are a live gap; if compare.py is only ever read by eye, they are noise.

selftest.sh's fresh run scored 4.353 b/B and the resume 4.231 at this size. Both are far above the order-0 anchor, which the file says is expected ('at this size they are noise'), but I have no way to confirm from the suite alone that the end-to-end run is training at all rather than just executing.

Is `bytes_per_id` / `maxlen` consistency (tok_test §3) sufficient to guarantee the bits/byte denominator, or does the denominator also depend on state the test does not reach? tok_test asserts the arrays agree; whether the reported bits/byte actually uses them is untested.
